answer: An exchange for summit forecasts, sable tracking and jetty traffic can give each agent one service quota per epoch only after a hash puzzle. Validators check that SHA-256 of the epoch beacon, public key and nonce falls below a fixed target, then mark that key's quota issued; invalid or repeated claims get no quota. Another identity requires a new search because the key changes the hash input. Parallel machines can shorten the wait but still pay the expected work per key. Security assumes unpredictable beacons and compute costs above the gain from another quota.
